topic: How does Face ID work in the dark?
title: How Face ID Sees You With the Lights Off 🔦
description: Face ID brings its own invisible light: an infrared flood illuminator and over 30,000 projected dots.
Dots on your nose land closer than on your cheeks — the warped pattern becomes a 3D map of your face.
sources: Wikipedia – Face ID (TrueDepth camera: dot projector with more than 30,000 infrared dots, flood illuminator, infrared camera): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face_ID

HuffPost UK – iPhone X Face ID: the infrared flood illuminator lets it work in the dark: https://huffingtonpost.co.uk/amp/entry/apples-iphone-x-face-id-heres-why-its-better-and-worse-than-a-fingerprint-sensor_uk_59b90196e4b02da0e13d8ff2

beats.narration: Face ID can see you in *total darkness*.
That's because it brings its own light: infrared, a color your eyes simply can't see.
First, a flood illuminator washes your face in *infrared*.
Then a projector fires over *30,000* invisible dots onto it.
Dots on your nose land closer than dots on your cheeks, so the pattern *warps*.
An infrared camera reads that warped pattern, builds a *3D map* of your face, and compares it with the one it stored.
All of this hides in the little black strip at the top of your screen.
Apple says the chance a random stranger unlocks it is about *one in a million*.
